how.title: How does the discount work?
how.body1: The program is called the Sliding Fee Discount Program. Health centers on this list receive federal funding (HRSA Health Center Program). In exchange, they are required by law to lower their prices for people with low income.
how.body2: It is not something you sign up for in advance. You ask for it at the clinic's front desk.
how.body3: The discount is based only on your income and household size. Savings, a car, or owning a home do not count.
how.body4: The discount applies only at that clinic. Each health center sets its own price list, so the same income can mean a different fee at a different clinic.
how.body5: This applies to federally funded health centers (FQHCs) — the clinics in this app. Free and charitable clinics work differently and are not included here yet.

verdict.full: You likely qualify for the largest discount — often free or a small flat fee. Ask for it.
verdict.partial: You likely qualify for a partial discount. Go ask — you will not know the exact price until they run your paperwork.
verdict.none: You likely will not get a sliding scale discount. But a health center still cannot deny you care, and their self-pay prices are usually far below hospital prices.

howToGet.title: How to get the discount
howToGet.step1: Ask at the front desk: "I'm uninsured — can I apply for the sliding fee discount?"
howToGet.step2: Fill out their form: household size and income.
howToGet.step3: Show proof of income — a pay stub, tax return, or a benefits letter.
howToGet.step4: You'll be given a set discounted price for your visits.
howToGet.warning: Without proof of income you will likely be charged the full price. Bring it with you.

hero.title: Get your price in writing
hero.subtitle: Before you go, you can ask any clinic for a written estimate of what your visit will cost. Federal law says they have to give it to you.

what.title: What is a Good Faith Estimate?
what.b1: A written estimate of your expected charges before a scheduled service.
what.b2: Required by the No Surprises Act (effective January 1, 2022) for uninsured and self-pay patients.
what.b3: It lists the main service plus related items the provider expects to bill — lab work, anesthesia, or facility fees.
what.b4: Must include the provider's name, NPI number, and the expected charge for each item.
what.b5: Free to request. No obligation to schedule.

how.title: How to get one
how.step1: Ask at scheduling — say you are uninsured or paying out of pocket and want a Good Faith Estimate.
how.step2: Request it in writing. The provider must give you the estimate in writing, not just a verbal quote.
how.step3: Keep the document. You will need it if the actual bill is higher than estimated.

timing.title: How quickly must they respond?

row1.label: Service scheduled 3 or more business days out
row1.value: Within 3 business days of your request

timing.note: These are minimum federal requirements. Some providers respond faster.

script.title: What to say
script.body: I'm paying out of pocket and I'd like a Good Faith Estimate in writing for [the service] before I schedule.
script.ifAskedBody: I don't have insurance. I'm paying out of pocket and I'm entitled to a Good Faith Estimate under the No Surprises Act.
script.ask2: Also ask: are there other providers involved — lab, anesthesiologist, radiologist? Request estimates from each.

fqhc.title: At sliding-scale clinics
fqhc.body1: Federally funded health centers (FQHCs) — the clinics in this app — are also required to provide Good Faith Estimates.
fqhc.body2: Their price is also based on your income. If you haven't estimated your sliding-scale discount yet, do that first — it will be more useful than a generic estimate.

dispute.title: If the bill is higher than the estimate
dispute.b1: You have the right to dispute if the final bill exceeds your Good Faith Estimate by more than $400.
dispute.b2: You must file within 120 days of receiving the bill.
dispute.b3: Ask the provider first — many billing errors are resolved without formal dispute.
dispute.b4: If the provider won't fix it, start an independent dispute resolution process.
dispute.b5: Contact CMS for help or to file:
dispute.b6: You do not have to pay the disputed amount while the review is open.

gfe.disclaimer: This is general information, not legal advice. The No Surprises Act applies to most U.S. providers but has exceptions. Rules may change. Verify current requirements at cms.gov or consult a patient advocate.

costs.title: What care usually costs without insurance
costs.subtitle: These are rough national ranges, not prices for any specific clinic. Sliding-scale clinics in this app are often much cheaper. Always call ahead to confirm your cost.
costs.primaryCareSub: Average around $160 nationwide. Retail and urgent care clinics often $80–250.
costs.labsSub: The same test can cost 3–10× more at a hospital. Always ask for the cash/self-pay price.
costs.fqhcSub: For low-income uninsured patients, often very little — or free. This is what most clinics in this app offer.
costs.whyBody: An ER visit without insurance averages about $2,715 — more than 10× a primary care visit. A community clinic can handle most non-emergencies for a fraction of that.
costs.disclaimer: Prices vary by region and provider and change over time. This is general information, not a quote or medical advice. Ranges based on 2025–2026 self-pay data. Call the clinic to confirm your cost.
costs.helpEntrySub: National price ranges for self-pay patients
costs.estimatorEntrySub: Low income can mean a small flat fee — or nothing at all

about.emergencyBody: This app is not for medical emergencies. If this is an emergency, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.
about.appDescription: Wellcott helps you find community health centers across the U.S. that accept self-pay and sliding-scale patients — no insurance required.
about.bringTitle: What to bring to your first visit
about.bringIncome: Proof of income (recent pay stub or benefits letter) — needed for the lowest sliding-scale fee
about.bringAddress: Proof of address (a utility bill or any mail)
about.bringMeds: A list of medications you take
about.bringNote: Without proof of income, a clinic may charge its standard rate until you can verify. If you don't have these, most clinics will still see you.
about.disclaimer1: Information is for reference only — not medical or legal advice.
about.disclaimer2: Prices vary. Most clinics use a sliding scale based on income — always call ahead to confirm.
about.disclaimer3: Federally funded health centers must see you regardless of insurance or ability to pay.
about.disclaimer4: Prescription savings are provided via SingleCare and are not insurance. We may earn a referral fee.
